text: Item 2. Management's Discussion and Analysis. Net sales were $94.9 billion, up 5% year over year. iPhone revenue was $46.2 billion. Services revenue reached $24.2 billion, up 14%. Gross margin was 46.2%. Operating cash flow was $28.9 billion. We returned $29 billion to shareholders via dividends and buybacks. Greater China sales declined 6%. We expect mid-single-digit revenue growth next quarter.

MD&A. Revenue was $64.7 billion, up 12%. Intelligent Cloud revenue $28.5 billion. Office Commercial products and cloud services grew 13%. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 29%. Operating income was $27.9 billion. Diluted EPS was $2.94. Capital expenditures were $14.9 billion, primarily servers and datacenters for AI.

Management Discussion. Net interest income was $22.9 billion. Noninterest revenue was $17.8 billion. Provision for credit losses was $3.1 billion. CET1 capital ratio was 15.0%. Average deposits were $2.4 trillion. Investment banking fees declined 8% versus the prior year. Card sales volume rose 7%.

Item 2. Earnings were $8.6 billion. Upstream production averaged 3.7 million oil-equivalent barrels per day. Downstream earnings were $1.2 billion. Capex was $6.1 billion. The company returned $9.2 billion to shareholders. Chemical margins compressed due to weaker industry pricing in Asia.

MD&A. Revenues of $98.9 billion, up 8%. UnitedHealthcare revenues $74.5 billion. Optum revenues $56.1 billion with intersegment eliminations. Operating earnings $7.9 billion. Medical care ratio was 84.8%. Days claims payable were 47.3. Membership grew to 53 million people served.

Management's Discussion. Revenue was $35.1 billion. Data Center revenue was $30.8 billion, up 154% year over year. Gross margin was 78.4%. Diluted EPS was $0.68 on a split-adjusted basis. Inventory was $8.3 billion. We saw strong demand for Hopper architecture GPUs for generative AI training.

Item 2. Sales were $23.1 billion. Innovative Medicine sales $14.0 billion. MedTech sales $8.0 billion. Adjusted EPS $2.71. R&D expense was $3.5 billion. Free cash flow was $4.8 billion. COVID-19 vaccine sales were negligible this quarter versus the prior year.

MD&A. Total revenue was $169.3 billion, up 4.8%. Walmart U.S. comparable sales rose 4.0%. eCommerce sales grew 22%. Operating income was $7.3 billion. Inventory increased 2% year over year. Membership income at Sam's Club rose 9%. Gross profit rate was 23.9%.

Item 2. Net sales were $20.9 billion, up 2%. Organic sales grew 3%. Operating income was $4.8 billion. Diluted net EPS was $1.37. Advertising expense was $2.4 billion. Gross margin expanded 80 basis points. Emerging markets organic sales grew 5%.

Management Discussion. Revenues were $16.9 billion. Commercial Airplanes delivered 126 airplanes. Defense, Space & Security revenue was $6.5 billion. Free cash flow was negative $3.9 billion. Research and development expense was $0.9 billion. We recorded charges related to the 777X program delay.
